execution/engine.notes: All 24 survivors are equivalent or unreachable. Three pass tool_calls=None instead of [] in the VOID, transport-failure and empty-response (T3-10) records: transcript.append writes None as []. One passes config=None to _build_messages, which does not use config. One replaces copy.deepcopy(messages) by copy.copy: the loop only appends to the list, never changes a message. Five change classify_attestation's arguments, which it ignores (always EV-1). Two drop the f'call_{turn}' default for a missing tool-call id and three change the '' default of tool_call_id in the tool message: a call without an id raises EngineError on the return-value lookup right after (S3-G2-2), so neither default is ever observed. Four change the defaults in current.get('choices', [{}])[0].get('message', {}) in the tool loop: only reached when the response has tool calls, so choices and message exist. Three change the '{}' default of arguments in _extract_calc_expression: None and 'XX{}XX' raise TypeError/JSONDecodeError, which are caught and give None, the same as '{}' (no expression). Two change the [] default of choices in _extract_tool_calls to None: both falsy, both give [].

execution/evidence.notes: All 8 survivors are equivalent. One changes ranks_above's default rank for an unknown first argument from -1 to -2; an unknown first argument never ranks above anything either way.

execution/perturbation_guard.notes: All 32 survivors are equivalent: each changes the 'base' or 'removed' detail of a tools, tool_choice or sampling diff (key name, or the value looked up). Those details are never observable: a violation always raises PerturbationRefusal, whose message uses only each diff's 'field' and 'issue', and the diff list is only ever returned empty. _summarise itself is tested directly. (Step 5 seal-gt-guards, T3-46: identical prompts now raise, and the identical-prompt diff entry is gone; its 14 mutants were all killed, so removing them lowered the score from 163/195 = 0.8359 to 149/181 = 0.8232 with the same 32 survivors.)

execution/version.notes: All 12 survivors are equivalent. Three touch dead code: the local 'modified' (False to None or True) and the first 'result = {}' are assigned and never read. Three change the unreachable else of 'parts[0] if parts else ...' (a stripped non-empty line always splits into at least one part). Five change how VERSION is opened or a path is encoded: 'UTF-8' is the same codec; no 'r', no encoding or encoding=None mean the locale's, UTF-8 on macOS and Linux. One opens 'version' instead of 'VERSION', which macOS's case-insensitive file system finds anyway. (Step 5 seal-verifier-hardening: the source hash covers src/ap1_run/ and VERSION only, F2/T3-70, and a VERSION commit under 7 characters marks the runner modified, S3-G3-2; the 12 survivors are the same ones; runner_environment, F2, has none.) foundation/config.notes: All 8 survivors are equivalent. Four change how config.json is opened: 'UTF-8' is the same codec, no 'r' is the default mode, and encoding None or no encoding means the locale's, which is UTF-8 on macOS and Linux (the tests load a non-ASCII config; on Windows these would be killed). Four change the .get() default for 'sampling' and 'quantisation' ({} to None or no default): both are required fields, checked present just before, so the default is never used.

foundation/numeric.notes: All 24 survivors are equivalent or unkillable. parse_decimal (7): is_neg=None is falsy like False; decimal_sep != 'XX.XX' only replaces '.' by '.'; the inner sign test 'XX-\u2212XX' only differs for 'X', which the outer test never lets through; sorting leading currency symbols by key=None or no key (4) is reverse alphabetical, and for startswith a symbol can only shadow another it is a prefix of, which sorts first either way. _build_extraction_re (2): key=None or no key for the alternation order is likewise equivalent (the regex backtracks; only a prefix can shadow). extract_numeric_tokens (9): currency_symbols=None reaches the same empty handling; finditer returns non-overlapping matches in order, so the dedup sort key (5 mutants) and last_end=-2 change nothing; every match contains a digit, so the 'no digits' guard and its continue->break (2) are unreachable. canonical_json ensure_ascii=None is falsy like False; canonical_hash 'UTF-8' is the same codec. file_hash (4): read(None) and read(8193) give the same digest; sentinel None or b'XXXX' never matches b'' and loops forever, which mutmut reports as a timeout. (Step 5 numeric-hardening: parse_decimal's R0.4.2 grammar check, quantise's places check, DECIMAL_CONTEXT, the operator reading of a sign after a number and _matches_inside_words added 132 mutants, all killed; the 'no digits' guard stays unreachable, as the token left after an operator always has digits.)
